packageRules.description: Image tag in the Helm chart is owned by CI (retag/promote release flow), never by Renovate
Go modules: one PR for all non-major bumps, majors stay separate for review
npm runtime deps: group non-major, majors separate
npm dev/tooling deps: group non-major, majors separate

Vite, its plugins, and vitest are version-locked (plugin-legacy@N needs vite@N, vitest peers on vite). Group every update type so a major lands as one coherent, installable PR instead of a broken standalone plugin bump.

Vector-tile stack is version-locked (@mapbox/vector-tile peers on pbf, both feed the PMTiles render path in web/src/lib/poi.ts). Group every update type so a coupled major lands as one installable PR.
GitHub Actions: one PR for all bumps (low-risk CI glue)
Container base images (Dockerfile + compose): one PR

Automerge non-major updates once every check on the PR head is green (none failing or pending; a skipped job counts as passed, so go, web, integration and e2e-ok all have to have passed or been skipped by the path filter), on any day, rebased onto the current main first. Renovate merges them itself on a later run instead of GitHub auto-merge (platformAutomerge off): main has no branch protection, so GitHub would merge before CI finished. A group containing a major is a major and stays manual. A release must be 3 days old before it is proposed or merged (minimumReleaseAge), the usual defence against a hijacked package release that is yanked within hours. A merge only reaches preview; prod still needs a release tag.
